summary: Bald Hill (Mount Ochepetuck), Union CT: Lawson's 1914 bungalow tower burned in 1942; state steel tower from 1957; register lists a former site.

facts.status_note: No source says whether the 1957 steel tower still stands. The register lists the site as a former lookout.

events.note: Plan being arranged for a trial lookout on Bald Hill in five towns, to pass fire messages by telephone
State set up an official fire station and made Mrs. Lawson its first observer
Fire tower built on Mrs. Lawson's bungalow at the summit; privately owned, publicly operated
December 1942 fire destroyed the tower and bungalow while Coast Artillery soldiers used it for observation
State erected a steel tower on the mountain; the fire observation center was again in operation
Register says the 60-foot steel tower was first operated in 1913; the Forest Lookouts history gives 1914 for the bungalow tower
Registered as Bald Hill Tower Site on September 9, 2008

evidence.supports: Bald Hill is also called Mt. Ochepituck; the hill is in Union
evidence.quote: A new fire tower will be erected on Bald Hill, also known as Mt. Ochepituck, off the Buckley Highway.

evidence.supports: Location: Union, Tolland County
evidence.quote: UNION - Tolland County

evidence.supports: 1910 plan for a trial lookout in five towns
evidence.quote: A plan is now being arranged to make a trial in the towns of Union, Woodstock, Ashford, Eastford and Stafford, by the establishment of a lookout

evidence.supports: Lookout was to pass fire messages by telephone
evidence.quote: This is to be a central point for the receipt and sending of messages by telephone concerning fires.

evidence.supports: Lawsons built a summer home on the mountain in 1906
evidence.quote: built a summer home on the mountain in 1906

evidence.supports: Mrs. Lawson began a voluntary fire-spotting service once a telephone was installed
evidence.quote: began a voluntary service of fire spotting

evidence.supports: About 1912 the state set up an official station; Mrs. Lawson first observer
evidence.quote: It was not until about 1912 that the State established a fire station officially and installed Mrs. Lawson as the pioneer fire observer.

evidence.supports: 1914 fire tower built on Mrs. Lawson's bungalow
evidence.quote: In 1914 Mrs. Lawson had a fire tower built on her bungalow on top of Mt. Ochepetuck.

evidence.supports: 1932 report: second fire observation in the state
evidence.quote: The second fire observation established in the state was Mt. Ochepetuck in Union with Mrs. Dedie Lawson, the owner, as observer.

evidence.supports: Observatory discontinued shortly before WWII
evidence.quote: Shortly before the World War II the fire observatory on Mt. Ochepetuck was discontinued.

evidence.supports: December 1942 fire destroyed tower and bungalow while Coast Artillery used the tower
evidence.quote: While soldiers of the Coast Artillery were using the tower for observation purposes in December, 1942, a fire destroyed the tower and bungalow.

evidence.quote: The fire tower will be located near the Bell Telephone Co. relay tower and will be supervised by the State Park and Forest Commission.

evidence.supports: 1957 the state had erected a steel tower southeast of the telephone relay station
evidence.quote: The state has erected a steel tower on the mountain, southeast of the telephone relay station.

evidence.supports: October 1957 the fire observation center was again in operation
evidence.quote: The forest fire observation center on Mt. Ochepetuck is again in operation.

evidence.supports: An observer served the fall season in 1957
evidence.quote: is serving as fire observer during the fall season

evidence.supports: Register: 60-foot steel tower first operated in 1913
evidence.quote: This 60' steel tower was first operated in 1913.

evidence.supports: Site is listed in the Former Fire Lookout Sites Register
evidence.quote: Former Fire Lookout Sites Register

evidence.supports: Register entry name is Bald Hill Tower Site
evidence.quote: Bald Hill Tower Site

evidence.supports: Entry registered September 9, 2008
evidence.quote: September 9, 2008

evidence.supports: A state telecommunications tower site off Bald Hill Road in Union, about 2,000 feet north of Route 190
evidence.quote: located off of Bald Hill Road at n existing Northeast Utilities tower site approximately 2,000 feet north from Route 190 in Union

notes_for_editor: Possible duplicate of data/research/us-ct-bald-hill.json (register 'Bald Hill Tower Site', CT 7, same hill name and county). Not merged; the editor should decide. Coordinates conflict: the record point 41.97379, -72.1982 matches the USGS GNIS summit 'Bald Hill' (41.974, -72.198), but the register point 41.785539, -72.268182 is about 21 km away, so the register may describe another hill. Dates conflict: register 1913 (steel tower) vs Forest Lookouts 1914 (bungalow tower). Forest Lookouts' 1957 steel tower may or may not be the register's tower. No source describes the site today. Status is unknown. The Forest Lookouts page quotes old newspapers and state reports, not the originals.
